title: Outlook: folder sharing respects organisation restrictions on Default and Anonymous permissions
summary: Hold: the Cloud Policy licensing guidance omits Microsoft's restriction that Microsoft 365 Apps for business supports only privacy-control policies, which matters when choosing how to enforce folder restrictions. The roadmap facts and registry instructions check out, but the promise that users can still edit named-user permissions goes beyond the roadmap's assurance that existing grants remain unaffected.

claims.claim: For the folder-permission Cloud Policy route, the briefing gives support for most Microsoft 365 plans including Microsoft 365 Apps without the Apps for business policy restriction.

Keep this general-control qualification separate from the still-unpublished licensing for the roadmap feature.
